# A test's component mounts at the first statement that is not setting it up
# (ir.TestSetup), on the interpreter as on every target. `var k = 5` and
# `t.assert(true)` are no setup, so the write after them is a write of the
# mounted component, which the effect hears. The interpreter mounted at the
# first read through the instance instead, so it took the write for the
# starting value and the effect heard nothing.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'
-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

component box ui.node {
    var count = 0
    var saved = 0

    ui.effect(
        on = count,
        @update(n) {
            saved += 1
        },
    )

    ui.text #out(value="{saved}")
}

func testLocalFirst(t test.Test, c box) {
    var k = 5
    c.count = k
    t.assert(c.saved == 1)
}

func testAssertFirst(t test.Test, c box) {
    t.assert(true)
    c.count = 5
    t.assert(c.saved == 1)
}

ui.window {
    box()
}
-- testrun/android/kotlin/app.sngl/box/1 --

    {
      "Desc": "AssertFirst",
      "Passed": true
    },
    {
      "Desc": "LocalFirst",
      "Passed": true
    }
  ]
}
